## edb55a59dc46

Version 3.0.0; SHA256 `b3068b1e8cf838e40afe90d836deb3df0f95a718f3d599e139c4e49f996c37e8`.

**Finding A3 — canonical test replay is in the ordinary sampling path.** The source embeds all five exact public inputs. `PUBLIC_PROFILES + GENERAL_PROFILES * 4` is the default weighted choice: one of its 45 entries is `public_5`, the exact canonical test input. Reproducer without overrides: `generate(10, 310, difficulty="medium")`.

```text
04700000000
00000000000
00000000000
00000000000
00000000900
00000000000
00000000000
00000000000
```

This is byte-equivalent as a normalized integer grid to the canonical test input. Its actual Racket output also equals the stored test output; all three are retained in audit_cases.json. The explicit override `generate(11, 29, scene_profile="public_5")` also reproduces it independently of seed.

Across seeds 0..999, sample_index=31*seed, difficulty=medium, **94/1,000** inputs exactly replay canonical inputs: train0=16, train1=21, train2=18, train3=12, test0=27. These are measured deterministic frequencies, not an exact probability estimate. The structural source-level test-replay weight is 1/45 under the declared default categorical draw.

This design is explicit in the existing source and is not characterized as covert leakage or unauthorized access. Canonical data are public in this packet. It is nevertheless a concrete contamination/replay risk if these samples are counted as novel synthetic training or the same task's canonical test is later presented as unseen evaluation. Suggested correction: default to procedural general profiles; keep exact-public profiles only in an opt-in, labeled replay/test suite and report their counts separately. Do not claim that removing public replay alone proves generalization.

Scope checked: all five canonical pairs and 90 generated general-profile cases (ten profiles x three bands x three seeds) matched real Racket and the local rule mirror. No incorrect label was observed. No target edit was made.
